249.title: Docker
249.content: The settings page edits this file under Docker as a form; “Advanced edit” opens it as text under Advanced. docker.yaml lists the Docker servers: for container: status labels on a service, and to discover services from container labels.

250.title: Servers
250.content: The Docker servers, for container: status labels and for discovery of labelled containers. Each top-level key is a name you choose (local, green, nas, …): . green: socket: /var/run/docker.sock # the socket as mounted in the dashboard's container nas: host: 192.168.1.20 # a Docker API or docker-socket-proxy port: 2375 protocol: http discover: false # only for container status, do not add its containers remote: host: docker.example.lan # the Docker daemon over TLS (dockerd --tlsverify, port 2376) port: 2376 tls: # homepage's keys; paths relative to the config folder caFile: tls/ca.pem certFile: tls/cert.pem keyFile: tls/key.pem . | Key | Default | What | . | socket |   | Path of a Docker socket inside the container. Mount it: /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro. :ro does not make the Docker API read-only (see Access below); a socket proxy does | . | host |   | Host name or IP of a Docker API or socket proxy (instead of socket) | . | port | 2375 | Port of that API | . | protocol | http | http or https (https when tls is set) | . | tls |   | caFile (the CA that signed the daemon’s certificate), certFile and keyFile (the client certificate, together). Read when the config loads; their contents stay on the server | . | discover | true | false: use the server for container: status only, without adding its containers | . | swarm | false | true: a Docker Swarm manager; discovery lists its services, and container: also finds a service by name (see Docker Swarm) | . | allowVariables | none | The {{DASHBOARD_VAR_*}} / {{DASHBOARD_FILE_*}} (and HOMEPAGE_) variables its containers’ labels may use, e.g. [DASHBOARD_VAR_GRAFANA], or true for all. See What labels may do | . The name is what server: refers to in services.yaml, and what config messages show. | No servers here (no file, or only comments): a socket mounted at /var/run/docker.sock is used as the server local by itself. For a single Docker host on the same machine, mounting the socket is all it takes. | One or more servers here: only those are used. To use the mounted socket next to another server, list it too, as green above. | One server: services with container: use it; server: is optional. Several servers: give such services server: <name>. Discovered containers always carry the server they were found on. | .

251.title: Discovery
251.content: Services can come from Docker labels and Kubernetes Ingress annotations as well as from services.yaml. Discovered services are merged into the groups. YAML wins: a discovered service with the same group and name as one in services.yaml is skipped. Discovered cards carry a small “auto” badge. Sources are polled every discovery.interval (default 30 s). Mount the Docker socket, or list a server in docker.yaml (see Servers): . # compose.yaml, the simplest form services: dashboard: image: ghcr.io/stefanrenne/dashboard:latest volumes: - ./config:/config - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro # :ro protects the file, not the API: see Access below . When docker.yaml lists no servers, a socket mounted at /var/run/docker.sock is used as the server local. Once it lists a server, only the listed ones are used; see Servers for names, several hosts and discover: false. The container starts as root only to give its node user the socket’s group, then runs the dashboard as node; no --group-add needed. Then label containers: . labels: dashboard.name: Grafana # required dashboard.group: Monitoring # default "Docker" dashboard.tab: Lab # the group's tab, unless settings.yaml layout gives it one (see Tabs) dashboard.icon: grafana.svg dashboard.href: http://grafana.lan dashboard.description: Dashboards dashboard.weight: "10" # order within the group, low first (default 0; services.yaml ones weigh 100, 200, ...) dashboard.siteMonitor: http://grafana:3000/api/health # otherwise: container state dashboard.widget.type: custom-api dashboard.widget.url: http://grafana:3000/api/health dashboard.widget.mappings: '[{"field":"version","label":"Version"}]' # JSON for lists and maps dashboard.widget.headers.Authorization: "Bearer {{DASHBOARD_VAR_GRAFANA}}" # dots make nested maps dashboard.statusStyle: dot # also target, showStats . The variable in the last widget label needs allowVariables: [DASHBOARD_VAR_GRAFANA] on the server in docker.yaml (see What labels may do). Several widgets and lists use homepage’s index notation: . labels: # Compose's list form: the same labels - dashboard.widgets[0].type=emby - dashboard.widgets[0].url=http://emby.lan - dashboard.widgets[1].type=custom-api - dashboard.widgets[1].url=http://argus.lan/api/v1/service/summary/emby - dashboard.widgets[1].mappings[0].label=Deployed version - dashboard.widgets[1].mappings[0].field.status=deployed_version . Several dashboards on one Docker host: give each an instanceName in settings.yaml. A label with instance.<name>. after the prefix applies to that dashboard only and wins over the plain label; the other dashboards ignore it. labels: dashboard.name: Emby dashboard.instance.internal.href: http://emby.lan dashboard.instance.public.href: https://emby.example.com . A discovered container always gets its Docker state as a status label, next to siteMonitor or ping when those are set. What labels may do . A label is written by whoever starts a container, and an image can bring labels of its own (a LABEL in its Dockerfile). So a discovered service gets less than one in services.yaml: . | Variables only where you allow them. {{DASHBOARD_VAR_*}} and {{DASHBOARD_FILE_*}} in a label are filled in only when the server’s allowVariables lists the variable (true: every one). Otherwise the service is left out, and the config messages name it. A label could otherwise send any of the dashboard’s passwords to a server of its own. | Nothing that runs or frames. Widget options marked discoverable: false (the button’s script, command, user and inheritEnv), options the page shows in a frame (the iframe’s src), provider: and references to another service’s widget (service_group / service_name) are dropped, with a message. target: hidden-iframe opens as a link instead of calling the address from the server. | What remains, such as a widget’s url, is called by the dashboard: a label can make it call an address in your network. Only people you trust should start containers on a discovered server; discover: false turns discovery off for a server. | . The same holds for Kubernetes annotations (allowVariables in kubernetes.yaml). Coming from homepage? Containers labelled for homepage (homepage.group + homepage.name, homepage.widget.*, …) are discovered as they are; {{HOMEPAGE_VAR_*}} in their labels is filled in from the environment when allowVariables lists it. dashboard.* labels win when a container has both. See From homepage for the rest of a move. Access. The dashboard only calls GET /containers/json and GET /containers/<name>/json|stats (with swarm: true also GET /services and /tasks). But :ro on a socket does not make the Docker API read-only: whoever can reach the socket can start and remove containers, which amounts to root on the host. Third-party widgets run inside the dashboard process, so they could reach it too. The safer setup is a docker-socket-proxy with only CONTAINERS=1, and host: docker-proxy in docker.yaml (see docker-compose.example.yml). A container started with --user (or Kubernetes runAsUser) skips the group step; give it the socket’s group yourself then: --group-add $(stat -c %g /var/run/docker.sock). Docker Swarm . Give the server swarm: true in docker.yaml, as in homepage. Discovery then lists the Swarm’s services instead of containers, so put the labels on the service (deploy.labels in a stack file), not on the container. Run the dashboard on a manager node (node.role == manager): only managers can list services. # stack.yaml, deployed with docker stack deploy -c stack.yaml media services: jellyfin: image: jellyfin/jellyfin deploy: labels: dashboard.name: Jellyfin dashboard.group: Media dashboard.href: http://jellyfin.lan . A service of a stack is named <stack>_<service> (media_jellyfin); that is its container: in services.yaml too. Its status label shows the running tasks against the replicas: running, partial (marked) or down, and CPU and memory when a running task is on the dashboard’s node. A container of that name still wins. With a socket proxy, also allow SERVICES=1 and TASKS=1.

253.title: Dockhand
253.content: type: dockhand · version 0.3.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . 307.title: Filters
307.content: filter: on a service in services.yaml hides its card while an expression is true; on one of its widgets it hides that widget. The expression reads the attributes its widgets and status checks publish: public values a widget declares for this (the Filter attributes table on each widget’s page lists them), apart from the blocks it shows. For example, a Shelly device that only appears while a firmware update is waiting: . - Devices: - Shelly Bureau: href: http://shelly-bureau.lan filter: widget.update == false # hidden while there is no update widget: type: shelly url: http://shelly-bureau.lan password: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_SHELLY_PASSWORD}}" .

308.title: The expression
308.content: . | An attribute: widget.<name> reads the attributes of all the service’s widgets together, so it works the same with one widget or several. When two widgets publish the same name, the first one on the card counts. To read one widget only: widgets[1].<name> (by position, from 0) or widgets.shelly.<name> (the first widget of that type). | A status check: container.<name>, ping.<name> and siteMonitor.<name> read the service’s container:, ping: or siteMonitor: check rather than a widget on the card (see Container health and Devices that do not answer). | A value: true, false, null, a number, 'text' or "text". | Comparing: ==, !=, <, <=, >, >= (< and > only between numbers). | Combining: && (and), || (or), ! (not), and parentheses: filter: widget.update == false && widget.queued == 0. | . A bare attribute is true while its value is: filter: ping.attention is the same as filter: ping.attention == true, and filter: "!ping.attention" the same as filter: ping.attention == false (in quotes: YAML reads a leading ! as a tag). The one difference: an attribute nobody sent is null, which ! counts as false and == false does not.

309.title: Attributes of the status checks
309.content: A service’s status checks publish these, whatever widgets it has. The attributes of a widget on the card differ per widget: see its page under Filter attributes. Most widgets also publish attention there, true while the card marks something as needing attention. container.<name>, the service’s container: (Docker): . | Attribute | Type | Value | . | attention | boolean | true while the container is unhealthy (its Docker healthcheck), stopped or not found | . | status | text | up, warn (running but unhealthy, or a Swarm service with too few tasks) or down | . ping.<name>, the service’s ping:: . | Attribute | Type | Value | . | attention | boolean | true while the host does not answer | . | status | text | up or down | . | latency | number | the answer time in ms; null without an answer | . siteMonitor.<name>, the service’s siteMonitor: (HTTP): . | Attribute | Type | Value | . | attention | boolean | true while it is not up: 5xx, another 4xx or no connection (2xx, 3xx and 401/403, a login in front of it, are up) | . | status | text | up, warn (another 4xx) or down | . | code | number | the HTTP status code, such as 200; null without a connection | . | latency | number | the answer time in ms; null without a connection | . Before a check has answered every attribute is null, and the card stays hidden; when the check itself fails, the card is shown.

310.title: While it waits, and when it fails
310.content: An attribute no widget sent counts as null, so widget.update == false is not true before the widget knows. Until the widgets the filter reads have answered, the card stays hidden; when one of them fails, the card is shown, so a broken service never disappears quietly. A group whose cards are all hidden is hidden too, and a hidden card is no search hit. While filters hide cards, the footer says how many (“3 hidden”); a click shows them, dimmed, until the next click.

311.title: Container health
311.content: Whether a service is healthy is decided by its container, not by a widget, so container.<name> reads the attributes of the service’s container: check: attention is true while the container is unhealthy (its Docker healthcheck), stopped or not found; a running container without a healthcheck is fine. To show a service only while something is wrong with it: . - Media: - Plex: href: http://plex.lan:32400 container: plex filter: container.attention == false # hidden while all is well; "!container.attention" works too . To tell unhealthy from stopped, container.status is warn for the one and down for the other. Discovered Docker services have container: already, so the label dashboard.filter=container.attention == false works there.

312.title: Devices that do not answer
312.content: ping.<name> reads the service’s ping: check: attention is true while the host does not answer. siteMonitor.<name> reads the HTTP check the same way: attention is true while it is not up. To hide a device while it is off: . - Living room: - Sonos: ping: sonos.lan filter: ping.attention # hidden while it does not answer . filter: ping.attention == false (or filter: "!ping.attention") does the opposite: the card only shows while the device is down.

313.title: A widget’s filter
313.content: filter: on one entry of widgets: hides that widget instead of the card, in the same language and reading the same attributes. For example a button that only shows while there is something to update: . - Docker: - Wud: widgets: - type: whatsupdocker url: http://wud:3000 - type: button text: Update containers filter: widgets.whatsupdocker.updates == 0 # hidden while there is nothing to update timeout: 900 command: >- curl -fsS http://wud:3000/api/containers | jq -r '.[] | select(.updateAvailable) | .id' | while read -r id; do curl -fsS -X POST "http://wud:3000/api/containers/$id/triggers/docker/update" >/dev/null || exit 1; done . The widget behaves as a filtered card: hidden until the widgets its filter reads have answered, and shown when one of them fails. A hidden widget keeps refreshing, since other filters may read it. The footer’s “hidden” is about whole cards: it does not count a hidden widget. It works on service widgets only (a header widget such as search keeps its own options), and a widget that has an option named filter itself keeps that option.

314.title: Discovered services
314.content: Discovered services take filters too: as the Docker label dashboard.filter (see Docker), or as the Kubernetes annotation getdashboard.dev/filter on an Ingress (see Kubernetes; getdashboard.dev/ is the annotations’ prefix, not a web address). A widget’s filter is dashboard.widgets[1].filter: . # compose.yaml: Compose's list form keeps the quotes and && of an expression simple labels: - dashboard.name=Shelly Bureau - dashboard.filter=widget.update == false # an Ingress metadata: annotations: getdashboard.dev/enabled: "true" getdashboard.dev/filter: widget.update == false .

315.title: Recipes
315.content: A filter hides a card while all is well, so the dashboard shows what needs a look: . - Media: - Radarr: # only while it marks something, such as a blocked import href: http://radarr.lan:7878 filter: widget.attention == false # or "!widget.attention" widget: { type: radarr, url: http://radarr.lan:7878, key: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_RADARR_KEY}}" } - Updates: # only while a container has an update filter: widget.updates == 0 widget: { type: whatsupdocker, url: http://wud.lan:3000 } - Infrastructure: - Proxmox: # only while a VM is stopped href: https://pve.lan:8006 filter: widget.vmsStopped == 0 widget: { type: proxmox, url: https://pve.lan:8006, username: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_PVE_USER}}", password: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_PVE_TOKEN}}" } - Speedtest: # only while the last test was slower than 100 Mbit/s filter: widget.download > 100 widget: { type: speedtest, url: http://speedtest.lan } - Uptime Kuma: # only while a monitor is down filter: widget.down == 0 widget: { type: uptimekuma, url: http://kuma.lan:3001, slug: home } - Plex: # only while its container is unhealthy or stopped container: plex filter: container.attention == false # or "!container.attention" - NAS: # only while it does not answer ping: nas.lan filter: ping.attention == false # or "!ping.attention" . The attributes each widget publishes are on its page under Filter attributes.

316.title: Mistakes
316.content: A mistake in the expression (widget.update false), a widget that is not on the service (widgets.radarr.queued on a Shelly), container.attention without container: or a secret in it are config errors; the service (or widget) is then shown unfiltered. An attribute the widget does not publish is a warning. The filter goes to the browser, so it cannot hold a {{DASHBOARD_VAR_*}} value.

342.title: FRITZ!Box

348.title: GameDig

Use the server’s query port in url (often the game port; Valheim and ARK use the game port + 1). For Minecraft use the minecraft widget. Learn more about Valve’s server query.

378.title: Glances
378.content: type: glances · version 0.4.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . CPU, memory, CPU temperature, uptime and disks of a machine that runs Glances in web server mode (glances -w, port 61208). Set version: 4 for Glances 4 or later. Give username and password only when Glances runs with --password. cputemp takes the hottest CPU sensor (labels starting with cpu_thermal, Core, Tctl, Temperature or Package id; add your own with cpuSensorLabel) and is marked from 85 °C. disk takes mount points as Glances lists them. CPU temperature, uptime and disks are off by default because each takes an extra call, as in homepage. Learn more about Glances.

379.content: cpu, memory, memoryUsed, memoryTotal, cputemp, uptime, disk (one mount point) or one per mount point named after it, diskFree . Pick them with fields: in the entry; without it the widget shows cpu, memory, cputemp, uptime.

406.title: HDHomeRun
406.content: type: hdhomerun · version 0.3.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . The channels (and HD channels) in an HDHomeRun’s lineup, the tuners in use, and for one tuner (tuner, from 0) the channel it plays, the signal strength and quality (marked below 50%), the client it streams to and the stream’s rate, as homepage’s hdhomerun widget. The tuner fields are empty while that tuner is idle. The device needs no key. Learn more about HDHomeRun.

407.title: Display fields
407.content: channels, hd, tunerCount, channelNumber, channelNetwork, signalStrength, signalQuality, symbolQuality, clientIP, networkRate . Pick them with fields: in the entry; without it the widget shows channels, hd.

408.title: Configuration options
408.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | E.g. http://hdhomerun.lan | . | tuner | number |   | 0 | The tuner for the tuner fields, from 0 | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

409.title: Filter attributes
409.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | channels | number | Channels in the lineup | . | hd | number | HD channels in the lineup | . | signalStrength | number | Signal strength of the tuner, in %; null while it is idle | . | signalQuality | number | Signal quality of the tuner, in %; null while it is idle | . | symbolQuality | number | Symbol quality of the tuner, in %; null while it is idle | . | networkRate | number | Bit rate the tuner streams, in Mbit/s; null while it is idle | . | attention | boolean | True while the card marks something as needing attention | .

410.title: Example
410.content: # services.yaml - Media: - HDHomeRun: href: http://hdhomerun.lan icon: hdhomerun widget: type: hdhomerun url: http://hdhomerun.lan tuner: 0 fields: [channels, tunerCount, channelNetwork, signalStrength] .

412.title: Header widgets
412.content: The settings page edits this file under Header widgets as a form; “Advanced edit” opens it as text under Advanced. widgets.yaml holds the widgets in the page’s header, above the groups: the date and time, system resources, a search box, the weather, and so on. Each list item is one widget, with its type as the key and its options below it. Every type is listed under Widgets. - datetime: dateStyle: full # full, long, medium, short, none timeStyle: short - resources: cpu: true memory: true disk: ["/", "/mnt/data"] cputemp: true # also uptime, network (true or an interface), expanded, units, diskUnits - search: provider: duckduckgo # duckduckgo, google, bing, startpage, baidu, brave, custom (+ url: https://x/?q={q}) showSearchSuggestions: true # suggestions while typing (google, duckduckgo, bing, baidu, brave; custom needs suggestionUrl) . With tabs, tab: puts a widget on one tab (tab: Lab) or several (tab: [Home, Lab]); without it, the widget is on every tab.

413.title: Widgets without a service
413.content: These widgets of the widgets collection are not tied to a service. Each widget has its own page with fields and an example under Widgets. | Type | Options | . | datetime | locale, dateStyle, timeStyle | . | greeting | text (required), text_size (xs … 4xl) | . | iframe | src (required; its origin is allowed in the page’s CSP), name, height or homepage’s classes, referrerPolicy, allowPolicy, allowFullscreen, loadingStrategy, allowScrolling, refreshInterval | . | logo | icon (optional; the dashboard’s own mark without it) | . | kubernetes | cluster (show, cpu, memory, showLabel, label), nodes (show, cpu, memory, showLabel); needs metrics-server and RBAC on nodes | . | search | provider, url, target, filterServices (default true: typing filters the services, Enter opens the only match) | . | resources | cpu, memory (both off by default), disk (list of mount points), label | . | http-status | url (required), method (HEAD/GET) | . | ping | host (required; a name, IP or URL) | . | docker | container (required), socket or url, swarm, tlsCa/tlsCert/tlsKey (secret) | . | kubernetes-pods | namespace, app or podSelector, and the connection from kubernetes.yaml (url, token, tlsCa, …) | . | proxmoxvm | node, vmid (required), type (qemu/lxc), and url, token, secret (secret), insecure from proxmox.yaml when left out | . | custom-api | url (required), method, headers (secret), body, display (block/list), mappings (required: field, label, format (number/percent/bytes/text), scale, prefix, suffix, remap: [{ value, to }, { any: true, to }]) | . The collection also has a widget for the weather (openmeteo, openweathermap), stocks, and every service homepage supports (radarr, sonarr, Unraid, Portainer, …).

415.title: Headscale
415.content: type: headscale · version 0.4.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . One node of Headscale: its name, first IP address, how long ago it was last seen and whether it is online (marked when not), as homepage’s headscale widget. Create an API key with headscale apikeys create and use it as key; headscale nodes list shows the node’s ID. Learn more about Headscale.

416.title: Display fields
416.content: name, address, last_seen, status . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

417.title: Configuration options
417.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | E.g. https://headscale.lan | . | nodeId | string | yes |   | The ID from headscale nodes list | . | key | string | yes |   | Secret: stays on the server. From headscale apikeys create | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

418.title: Filter attributes
418.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | status | string | Online or offline | . | hoursSinceSeen | number | Hours since the node was last seen; 0 while online, null when never | . | attention | boolean | True while the card marks something as needing attention | .

419.title: Example
419.content: # services.yaml - Network: - Headscale: icon: headscale widget: type: headscale fields: [name, address, last_seen, status] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults url: https://headscale.lan nodeId: 3 key: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_HEADSCALE_KEY}}" .

421.title: Health checks
421.content: type: healthchecks · version 0.3.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . The checks that are up and down (marked) in a Healthchecks.io project, or with uuid one check’s state (down and in its grace period marked) and how long ago it last pinged, as homepage’s healthchecks widget. Create a key in your project under Settings > API Access > Create API key (read-only is enough) and use it as key. Works with a self-hosted Healthchecks and with healthchecks.io. Learn more about Healthchecks.

422.title: Display fields
422.content: up, down, status, last_ping . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

423.title: Configuration options
423.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | E.g. https://healthchecks.lan (or https://healthchecks.io) | . | key | string | yes |   | Secret: stays on the server. Project Settings > API Keys (read-only is enough) | . | uuid | string |   |   | One check; without it the totals of all checks | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

424.title: Filter attributes
424.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | up | number | Checks up | . | down | number | Checks down | . | attention | boolean | True while the card marks something as needing attention | .

425.title: Example
425.content: # services.yaml - Monitoring: - Backups ping: href: https://healthchecks.lan icon: healthchecks widget: type: healthchecks fields: [up, down, status, last_ping] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults url: https://healthchecks.lan key: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_HEALTHCHECKS_KEY}}" uuid: 5f1c3a2e-8b7d-4e6f-9a0b-1c2d3e4f5a6b .

427.title: Home Assistant
427.content: type: homeassistant · version 0.3.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . People at home, lights that are on and switches that are on (each as “on / all”), as homepage’s homeassistant widget. With custom, up to four entries of your own instead, in homepage’s form: . | state: <entity_id> shows that entity. label defaults to {attributes.friendly_name}, value to {state} {attributes.unit_of_measurement}; both may name other attributes in braces. | template: <Jinja template> shows what Home Assistant renders, with your label. | . Make a long-lived access token in Home Assistant: your profile (bottom left) > Security > Long-lived access tokens > Create token. The token can read everything its user can. Learn more about Home Assistant.

428.title: Display fields
428.content: people_home, lights_on, switches_on; with custom: custom1 to custom4 . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

429.title: Configuration options
429.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | E.g. http://homeassistant.lan:8123 | . | key | string | yes |   | Secret: stays on the server. A long-lived access token: your profile > Security | . | custom | list |   |   |   | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

430.title: Filter attributes
430.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | peopleHome | number | People at home (without custom) | . | lightsOn | number | Lights that are on (without custom) | . | switchesOn | number | Switches that are on (without custom) | . | custom1 | string | The first custom entry’s value, as the card shows it (e.g. “on”, “21.5 °C”) | . | custom2 | string | The second custom entry’s value | . | custom3 | string | The third custom entry’s value | . | custom4 | string | The fourth custom entry’s value | .

431.title: Example
431.content: # services.yaml - Home: - Home Assistant: href: http://homeassistant.lan:8123 icon: home-assistant widget: type: homeassistant fields: [people_home, lights_on, switches_on, custom, custom1, custom4] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults url: http://homeassistant.lan:8123 key: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_HASS_TOKEN}}" custom: # optional: instead of people, lights and switches - state: sensor.total_power - state: sensor.energy_today label: Energy today - template: "{{ states.switch | selectattr('state', 'eq', 'on') | list | count }}" label: Switches on - state: weather.home label: Wind value: "{attributes.wind_speed} {attributes.wind_speed_unit}" .

433.title: Homebox
433.content: type: homebox · version 0.3.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . The items in your Homebox inventory, their total value (in the currency set in Homebox), and with fields the items under warranty, locations, labels and users, as homepage’s homebox widget. The widget logs in with the e-mail address and password you use on the web. Learn more about Homebox.

434.title: Display fields
434.content: items, totalWithWarranty, locations, labels, users, totalValue . Pick them with fields: in the entry; without it the widget shows items, locations, totalValue.

435.title: Configuration options
435.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | E.g. http://homebox.lan:7745 | . | username | string | yes |   | The e-mail address you log in with | . | password | string | yes |   | Secret: stays on the server. | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

436.title: Filter attributes
436.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | items | number | Items in the inventory | . | totalWithWarranty | number | Items under warranty | . | locations | number | Locations | . | labels | number | Labels | . | users | number | Users | .

437.title: Example
437.content: # services.yaml - Home: - Homebox: href: http://homebox.lan:7745 icon: homebox widget: type: homebox fields: [items, totalWithWarranty, locations, labels, users, totalValue] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults url: http://homebox.lan:7745 username: anna@example.com password: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_HOMEBOX_PASSWORD}}" .

439.title: Homebridge
439.content: type: homebridge · version 0.4.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . Whether Homebridge is up (marked when not), whether an update for Homebridge or one of its plugins is available (marked), and the child bridges that run of all of them (when there are any), as homepage’s homebridge widget. The API comes from the Homebridge UI (homebridge-config-ui-x, part of Homebridge); the widget logs in with a user of that UI. Learn more about Homebridge.

440.title: Display fields
440.content: status, updates, child_bridges . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

441.title: Configuration options
441.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | Homebridge UI, e.g. http://homebridge.lan:8581 | . | username | string | yes |   |   | . | password | string | yes |   | Secret: stays on the server. | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

442.title: Filter attributes
442.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | status | string | Homebridge’s state: up, pending or down | . | update | boolean | True when Homebridge or a plugin has an update | . | attention | boolean | True while the card marks something as needing attention | .

443.title: Example
443.content: # services.yaml - Home: - Homebridge: href: http://homebridge.lan:8581 icon: homebridge widget: type: homebridge fields: [status, updates, child_bridges] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults url: http://homebridge.lan:8581 username: admin password: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_HOMEBRIDGE_PASSWORD}}" .

445.title: From homepage
445.content: Dashboard reads homepage’s configuration as it is: its files, its Docker labels and Kubernetes annotations, and its variables. Moving over is mostly a matter of swapping the image.

446.title: Switch the container
446.content: # compose.yaml services: - homepage: - image: ghcr.io/gethomepage/homepage:latest + dashboard: + image: ghcr.io/stefanrenne/dashboard:latest ports: - 3000:3000 volumes: - - ./config:/app/config + - ./config:/config # the same folder, at another path - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro environment: HOMEPAGE_VAR_RADARR_KEY: 0123456789abcdef # keeps working, as do HOMEPAGE_FILE_* - HOMEPAGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS: dash.lan # not read: add the name on the settings page . On its first start the dashboard installs its widgets, the widgets collection, from GitHub, so the container needs to reach github.com. It reads only from Docker: give it a docker-socket-proxy rather than the socket itself.

447.title: What carries over as it is
447.content: | homepage | In Dashboard | . | services.yaml | Groups and nested groups; href, icon, description, siteMonitor, ping, container with server, app with namespace and podSelector, proxmoxNode with proxmoxVMID; widget: and widgets: with fields, refreshInterval, hide_errors, highlight and provider | . | widgets.yaml | The info widgets: datetime, greeting, logo, openmeteo, openweathermap, resources, search, kubernetes, glances, longhorn, stocks, unifi_console | . | bookmarks.yaml | As it is | . | settings.yaml | layout (columns, style, tabs, nested groups), theme, color, background, cardBlur, quicklaunch, providers, statusStyle, showStats, target, hideVersion, … (see Settings) | . | docker.yaml, kubernetes.yaml, proxmox.yaml | The same servers, cluster and nodes | . | homepage.* Docker labels | Discovered as they are (see Docker) | . | gethomepage.dev/* annotations | Discovered as they are (see Kubernetes) | . | {{HOMEPAGE_VAR_*}}, {{HOMEPAGE_FILE_*}} | Filled in from the environment, and kept secret (see Variables) | . | icons/ | icon: /icons/name.svg as before | . Every homepage service widget has a counterpart in the widgets collection under the same name, also homepage’s own spellings such as customapi, overseerr, jellyseerr, unifi_console and unifi_drive. Each widget’s page lists its options.

448.title: What is different
448.content: . | custom.css and custom.js are loaded as in homepage, but the page underneath is another one: selectors written for homepage’s markup do not match. Rewrite them against the dashboard’s theme properties (--dash-card, --dash-text, …) and classes (see Custom CSS & JS). | Allowed hosts are checked as in homepage, but they live in settings.yaml (allowedHosts, or the settings page) instead of HOMEPAGE_ALLOWED_HOSTS, which is not read. Unlike homepage, IP addresses always work (see Allowed hosts). | Variables in labels ({{HOMEPAGE_VAR_*}} in a homepage.* label or annotation) are filled in only when the server in docker.yaml, or kubernetes.yaml, lists them under allowVariables: (true for all, as homepage does); otherwise the service is left out with a message. Buttons and frames from labels are refused (see What labels may do). | Widgets are packages. They come from the widgets collection, which updates itself to its newest release; plugins: in settings.yaml pins a release or adds widgets of others (see Settings). | .

449.title: Once you are over
449.content: Nothing has to change: the homepage forms keep working. Dashboard’s own names sit next to them for new configuration: {{DASHBOARD_VAR_*}} and {{DASHBOARD_FILE_*}}, Docker labels dashboard.* and Kubernetes annotations getdashboard.dev/*. And there is more than homepage has: filters that show a card only while something needs a look, buttons that run a script, !include to split up a long services.yaml (see Including other files), and widgets anyone can publish (see Extend).

451.title: HTTP status
451.content: type: http-status · version 1.3.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . Checks that a URL answers and shows the status code and response time. This is the widget behind a service’s siteMonitor:; use it directly for a second URL or to show the blocks. HEAD is the default; use GET for servers that do not answer HEAD properly.

452.title: Display fields
452.content: status, latency . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

453.title: Configuration options
453.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   |   | . | method | HEAD / GET |   | HEAD |   | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

454.title: Filter attributes
454.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | status | string | Up or down, as the status label | . | code | number | The HTTP status code, such as 200 | . | latency | number | Time the URL took to answer, in ms | . | attention | boolean | True while the card marks something as needing attention | .

455.title: Example
455.content: # services.yaml - Infrastructure: - Router: href: https://router.lan siteMonitor: https://router.lan # the status label in the corner widget: type: http-status fields: [status, latency] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults url: https://router.lan/api/health method: GET .

457.title: iFrame
457.content: type: iframe · version 1.1.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . Another page in a frame on the card, as homepage’s iframe widget: a Grafana panel, a camera page, a status page. The dashboard allows the page’s origin (scheme, host and port of src) in its Content-Security-Policy; every other origin stays blocked. Your browser loads the page itself, so it must be reachable from the browser, and the page must allow being framed (no X-Frame-Options: DENY or frame-ancestors that leaves the dashboard out). height sets the frame’s height (default 15rem); homepage’s classes are read for their height (h-60 is 15rem, the last h-<n> counts). allowScrolling: no makes the page a picture that cannot be scrolled or clicked, and refreshInterval reloads it every so many milliseconds.

458.title: Display fields
458.content: No blocks: the frame is drawn by the widget.

459.title: Configuration options
459.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | src | url | yes |   | The page, e.g. https://grafana.lan/d-solo/abc?panelId=2 | . | name | string |   |   | The frame’s title for screen readers | . | height | string |   |   | A CSS height, e.g. 20rem (default 15rem) | . | classes | string |   |   | Homepage’s Tailwind height classes; the h- of the largest screen is used | . | referrerPolicy | string |   |   | E.g. same-origin | . | allowPolicy | string |   |   | The frame’s allow attribute, e.g. autoplay; fullscreen | . | allowFullscreen | boolean |   | true |   | . | allowfullscreen | boolean |   |   | Homepage’s spelling of allowFullscreen | . | loadingStrategy | eager / lazy |   | eager |   | . | allowScrolling | yes / no |   | yes | No: the page cannot be scrolled or clicked | . | refreshInterval | number |   |   | Reload the page every this many milliseconds (at least 1000) | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

460.title: Example
460.content: # services.yaml - Monitoring: - Power use: widget: type: iframe name: Power use src: https://grafana.lan/d-solo/power?orgId=1&panelId=2 height: 12rem allowScrolling: "no" refreshInterval: 60000 .

462.title: Images
462.content: Wherever the config takes an icon (a service’s icon, a bookmark, a group’s icon in layout, favicon, a widget option of type icon), it takes the same forms, as in homepage. Most icons come from a free icon set on a CDN; the browser loads them from there, the dashboard itself does not. | Form | Provider | Browse | . | plex, plex.svg, plex.webp | Dashboard Icons by Homarr: logos of self-hosted apps (png without an extension) | dashboardicons.com | . | sh-plex, sh-plex.svg, sh-plex.webp | selfh.st icons: logos of self-hosted apps (png without an extension) | selfh.st/icons | . | mdi-flask-outline | Material Design Icons by Pictogrammers: general-purpose symbols | pictogrammers.com/library/mdi | . | si-plex | Simple Icons: brand logos | simpleicons.org | . | /icons/<file> | Your own: a file in the icons folder of your config |   | . | https://... | Any image on the web |   | . # services.yaml - Media: - Plex: icon: plex.svg # Dashboard Icons, as svg - Jellyfin: icon: sh-jellyfin # selfh.st icons, as png - Backups: icon: mdi-backup-restore-#4ade80 # Material Design Icons, in green - GitHub: icon: si-github # Simple Icons - Dashboard: icon: dashboard.svg # Dashboard's own icon, on Dashboard Icons - Garage door: icon: /icons/garage.svg # config/icons/garage.svg - Camera: icon: https://example.com/camera.png .

463.title: Colours of single-colour icons
463.content: mdi- and si- icons are single-coloured. They follow iconStyle in settings.yaml: gradient (the default, the accent colour as a gradient) or theme (flat, in the theme’s text colour). Or give one its own colour as a suffix: mdi-flask-outline-#f0d453, si-plex-#e5a00d.

464.title: Your own icons
464.content: Put image files (svg, png, webp, …) in an icons folder in your config folder and use them as /icons/<file>, also in subfolders (/icons/brands/nas.svg). The dashboard serves only that folder. Nothing is fetched from elsewhere, so this also works without internet access.

465.title: Background image
465.content: background in settings.yaml takes a URL or a file in icons/ (background: /icons/wallpaper.jpg), with optional blur, saturation, brightness and opacity. cardBlur frosts the cards over it.

467.title: Immich
467.content: type: immich · version 0.4.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . The number of users, photos and videos and the storage they use, as homepage’s immich widget. Set version: 2 for Immich 1.118 or later (homepage’s default is 1). Make an API key as an admin under Account Settings > API Keys, with at least the permission server.statistics. Learn more about Immich.

468.title: Display fields
468.content: users, photos, videos, storage . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

469.title: Configuration options
469.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | E.g. http://immich.lan:2283 | . | key | string | yes |   | Secret: stays on the server. An admin’s API key with server.statistics: Account Settings > API Keys | . | version | number |   | 1 | 2 for Immich 1.118 or later, as in homepage | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

470.title: Filter attributes
470.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | users | number | Users | . | photos | number | Photos | . | videos | number | Videos | . | storage | number | Space the photos and videos take, in GB | .

471.title: Example
471.content: # services.yaml - Media: - Immich: href: http://immich.lan:2283 icon: immich widget: type: immich fields: [users, photos, videos, storage] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults url: http://immich.lan:2283 key: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_IMMICH_KEY}}" version: 2 .

473.title: Service widgets
473.content: Widgets on a service’s card, under widget: in services.yaml. From the widgets collection develop, always installed. | Widget | type | What it shows | . | AdGuard Home | adguard | DNS queries, blocked and filtered queries and the processing time of AdGuard Home (homepage’s adguard widget). | . | APC UPS | apcups | Status, load, battery charge and runtime left of an APC UPS through apcupsd (homepage’s apcups widget). | . | Arcane | arcane | Containers running, stopped and in total, images and image updates in Arcane (homepage’s arcane widget). | . | Argo CD | argocd | Applications by sync and health status in Argo CD (homepage’s argocd widget). | . | Atsumeru | atsumeru | Series, archives, chapters and categories in Atsumeru (homepage’s atsumeru widget). | . | Audiobookshelf | audiobookshelf | Podcasts and books in Audiobookshelf, with their total length (homepage’s audiobookshelf widget). | . | authentik | authentik | Users, and logins, failed logins and (version 2) authorizations of the last 24 hours in authentik (homepage’s authentik widget). | . | autobrr | autobrr | Approved and rejected pushes, filters and indexers in autobrr (homepage’s autobrr widget). | . | Azure DevOps | azuredevops | The last run of a pipeline, and open pull requests in a repository (homepage’s azuredevops widget). | . | Backrest | backrest | The latest backups that succeeded and failed, and the last 30 days of Backrest’s plans (homepage’s backrest widget). | . | Bazarr | bazarr | Episodes and movies that still miss subtitles. | . | Beszel | beszel | Systems up of all in Beszel, or the status, CPU, memory, disk and network of one system (homepage’s beszel widget). | . | BookLore | booklore | Libraries, books, books you are reading and finished in BookLore (homepage’s booklore widget). | . | BookOrbit | bookorbit | Books, authors, and books you are reading and finished in BookOrbit (homepage’s bookorbit widget). | . | Button | button | A button that opens a link or runs a script or shell command on the dashboard’s server. | . | Caddy | caddy | Reverse proxy upstreams, their requests and failed requests from Caddy’s admin API (homepage’s caddy widget). | . | Calendar | calendar | A month or an agenda with releases from Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr and Readarr and events from iCal feeds (homepage’s calendar widget). | . | Calibre-Web | calibreweb | Books, authors, categories and series in Calibre-Web (homepage’s calibreweb widget). | . | changedetection.io | changedetectionio | Watches with an unseen change, and all watches, in changedetection.io (homepage’s changedetectionio widget). | . | Channels DVR Server | channelsdvrserver | Shows, recordings, scheduled recordings and passes of a Channels DVR Server (homepage’s channelsdvrserver widget). | . | Checkmk | checkmk | Services and hosts that are not OK in a Checkmk site (homepage’s checkmk widget). | . | Cloudflare Tunnel | cloudflared | The status and origin IP of a Cloudflare Tunnel (homepage’s cloudflared widget). | . | CoinMarketCap | coinmarketcap | 477.title: Jackett
477.content: type: jackett · version 0.3.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . The configured indexers and how many of them failed on their last search (marked), as homepage’s jackett widget. key is the API Key at the top of Jackett’s page. When Jackett has an Admin password set, give it as password too. Learn more about Jackett.

478.title: Display fields
478.content: configured, errored . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

479.title: Configuration options
479.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | E.g. http://jackett.lan:9117 | . | key | string | yes |   | Secret: stays on the server. The API Key at the top of Jackett’s page | . | password | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. The admin password, when one is set | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

480.title: Filter attributes
480.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | configured | number | Indexers configured | . | errored | number | Configured indexers whose last search failed | . | attention | boolean | True while the card marks something as needing attention | .

481.title: Example
481.content: # services.yaml - Downloads: - Jackett: href: http://jackett.lan:9117 icon: jackett widget: type: jackett fields: [configured, errored] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults url: http://jackett.lan:9117 key: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_JACKETT_KEY}}" password: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_JACKETT_PASSWORD}}" # only with an admin password .

483.title: JDownloader
483.content: type: jdownloader · version 0.4.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . The packages in JDownloader’s download list, their total size, what is left to download and the download rate, as homepage’s jdownloader widget. Like homepage it goes through My.JDownloader: connect JDownloader to your account under Settings > My.JDownloader, then fill in the account’s e-mail address and password and the device name shown there as client. JDownloader needs no open port for this. Learn more about JDownloader.

484.title: Display fields
484.content: downloadCount, downloadTotalBytes, downloadBytesRemaining, downloadSpeed . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

485.title: Configuration options
485.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | username | string | yes |   | The e-mail address of your My.JDownloader account | . | password | string | yes |   | Secret: stays on the server. | . | client | string | yes |   | The device name of the JDownloader instance (Settings > My.JDownloader) | . | url | url |   | https://api.jdownloader.org | Only for another My.JDownloader server | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

486.title: Filter attributes
486.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | downloadCount | number | Packages in the download list | . | downloadBytesRemaining | number | Still to download over all packages, in GB | . | downloadSpeed | number | Download speed of the running packages, in MB/s | .

487.title: Example
487.content: # services.yaml - Downloads: - JDownloader: href: https://my.jdownloader.org/ icon: jdownloader widget: type: jdownloader fields: [downloadCount, downloadTotalBytes, downloadBytesRemaining, downloadSpeed] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults username: anna@example.com password: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_MYJD_PASSWORD}}" client: JDownloader@nas .

489.title: Jellyfin
489.content: type: jellyfin · version 0.3.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . What is playing on Jellyfin, one row per stream with its position and a progress bar (paused streams get a pause icon), as homepage’s jellyfin widget. With enableBlocks: true it also shows the number of movies, series, episodes, songs and albums; enableNowPlaying: false leaves the streams out. Pausing a stream from the card (homepage’s enableMediaControl) is not offered: the widgets only read. Make an API key in Jellyfin under Dashboard > API Keys (Jellyfin 10.12: Administration > Dashboard > Advanced > API Keys). homepage’s version: 2 is accepted but not needed. Learn more about Jellyfin.

490.title: Display fields
490.content: movies, series, episodes, songs, albums . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

491.title: Configuration options
491.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | E.g. http://jellyfin.lan:8096 | . | key | string | yes |   | Secret: stays on the server. Dashboard > API Keys | . | enableNowPlaying | boolean |   | true | A row per stream that is playing | . | enableBlocks | boolean |   | false | Movies, series, episodes, songs and albums | . | enableUser | boolean |   | false | The user’s name after the title | . | showEpisodeNumber | boolean |   | false | S01 · E02 in episode titles | . | version | number |   | 1 | Homepage’s option for Jellyfin 10.12; not needed here (both versions work) | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

492.title: Filter attributes
492.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | streams | number | Streams playing now | .

493.title: Example
493.content: # services.yaml - Media: - Jellyfin: href: http://jellyfin.lan:8096 icon: jellyfin widget: type: jellyfin fields: [movies, series, episodes, songs, albums] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults url: http://jellyfin.lan:8096 key: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_JELLYFIN_KEY}}" enableBlocks: true enableUser: true showEpisodeNumber: true .

543.title: Kubernetes
543.content: The settings page edits this file under Kubernetes as a form; “Advanced edit” opens it as text under Advanced. kubernetes.yaml connects the dashboard to a cluster: to discover services from Ingress, IngressRoute and HTTPRoute annotations, for app: pod status labels on a service, and for the Kubernetes header widget. mode: cluster # in the cluster (its service account); default: a kubeconfig; disabled (when unset) kubeconfig: kube/config # mode: default only; relative to the config folder. Else $KUBECONFIG or ~/.kube/config context: home # mode: default only; else the kubeconfig's current context ingress: true # discover Ingresses (default true) traefik: false # discover Traefik IngressRoutes gateway: false # discover Gateway API HTTPRoutes . See Discovery below. The kubernetes widget uses the same connection.

544.title: Discovery
544.content: Services can come from Docker labels and Kubernetes Ingress annotations as well as from services.yaml. Discovered services are merged into the groups. YAML wins: a discovered service with the same group and name as one in services.yaml is skipped. Discovered cards carry a small “auto” badge. Sources are polled every discovery.interval (default 30 s). kubernetes.yaml: mode: cluster in the cluster, or mode: default outside it (as in homepage). With mode: cluster the dashboard uses its service account to list Ingresses in all namespaces; with mode: default it reads a kubeconfig instead: kubeconfig: (a path relative to the config folder), else $KUBECONFIG, else ~/.kube/config, with its current context or context:. # kubernetes.yaml, the dashboard in Docker next to a cluster mode: default kubeconfig: kube/config # /config/kube/config in the container context: home # optional: another context than the current one . A kubeconfig may hold a token (token, tokenFile), a client certificate (client-certificate / client-key, or their -data forms) or a user name and password. Credential plugins (exec, as for EKS, GKE and AKS) are not run: make a service account token for the dashboard instead (kubectl create token dashboard --duration=8760h) and put it in the kubeconfig. Give that account the RBAC below. In the cluster: The image starts as root and drops to node itself; with runAsNonRoot: true in the pod’s security context, also set runAsUser: 1000. RBAC: . apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: ClusterRole metadata: { name: dashboard } rules: - apiGroups: ["networking.k8s.io"] resources: ["ingresses"] verbs: ["list"] # pod status labels (app:, and discovered services) - apiGroups: ["", "metrics.k8s.io"] resources: ["pods"] verbs: ["list"] # only with traefik: true - apiGroups: ["traefik.io", "traefik.containo.us"] resources: ["ingressroutes"] verbs: ["list"] # only with gateway: true - apiGroups: ["gateway.networking.k8s.io"] resources: ["httproutes", "gateways"] verbs: ["list", "get"] --- apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1 kind: ClusterRoleBinding metadata: { name: dashboard } roleRef: { apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io, kind: ClusterRole, name: dashboard } subjects: [{ kind: ServiceAccount, name: dashboard, namespace: homelab }] . Annotate Ingresses: . metadata: annotations: getdashboard.dev/enabled: "true" # required getdashboard.dev/name: Grafana # default: the Ingress name getdashboard.dev/group: Monitoring # default: the namespace getdashboard.dev/tab: Lab # the group's tab (see Tabs) getdashboard.dev/icon: grafana.svg getdashboard.dev/href: https://grafana.example.com # default: first rule host + path (https with TLS) getdashboard.dev/widget.type: http-status getdashboard.dev/widget.url: http://grafana.monitoring:3000/api/health . homepage’s gethomepage.dev/* annotations work as well. Annotations get what Docker labels get (see What labels may do): {{DASHBOARD_VAR_*}} in them is filled in only for the variables allowVariables: in kubernetes.yaml lists (true: all), and options that run or frame something come from services.yaml only. Pod status. As in homepage, a discovered Ingress or route gets the state of its app’s pods as a label (the Kubernetes pods widget): the pods labelled app.kubernetes.io/name=<its name> in its namespace. getdashboard.dev/app names another app, getdashboard.dev/pod-selector takes a label selector, and getdashboard.dev/external: "true" leaves the label out. This needs list on pods (and pods.metrics.k8s.io for CPU and memory). Traefik and the Gateway API, as in homepage: Ingresses are listed by default; add traefik: true for Traefik’s IngressRoutes (traefik.io and the older traefik.containo.us) and gateway: true for Gateway API HTTPRoutes to kubernetes.yaml, ingress: false to skip Ingresses. They take the same annotations. Without href, an IngressRoute links to the host and path of its first Host(...) match (https with tls), and an HTTPRoute to its first hostname and path, https when its Gateway’s listener is HTTPS. A kind that is not installed is skipped. # kubernetes.yaml mode: cluster traefik: true gateway: true .

558.title: A local widget
558.content: A local widget is a folder on the machine that runs the dashboard. The dashboard runs it as it is: no repository, no release. It is the quickest way to a widget of your own, and the way to try one out while you write it.

559.title: 1. Make the folder
559.content: Copy examples/widget-template into your config folder, for example as my-widgets/my-nas. Or, in a clone of the dashboard: . npm run new-widget -- my-nas ./config/my-widgets/my-nas . That copies the template with example-counter renamed to my-nas everywhere: the id and name in widget.yaml, the dash-<id> element in client.js, the README and the tests.

560.title: 2. Declare the options
560.content: Every option you read goes into options: in widget.yaml. Mark API keys, passwords and tokens secret: true. Users fill them in with {{DASHBOARD_VAR_...}}, but the flag is what keeps them out of the browser even when someone types the key in directly. # widget.yaml id: my-nas name: My NAS version: 1.0.0 apiVersion: 2 description: Free space and running jobs of the NAS. options: url: { type: url, required: true } # e.g. http://nas.lan:5000 key: { type: string, secret: true, required: true } .

561.title: 3. Write fetch(ctx)
561.content: Fetch from the service with ctx.fetch, then return blocks: . export default { async fetch(ctx) { const res = await ctx.fetch('/api/summary', { headers: { 'X-Api-Key': ctx.options.key } }); if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`answered ${res.status}`); const s = await res.json(); return { status: 'up', blocks: [ { label: 'queries', value: s.queries }, { label: 'blocked', value: s.blocked_percentage, unit: '%' }, ], }; }, }; . Guidelines: . | Throw an error with a short, useful message. It appears on the card. | Keep it fast; the call is aborted after 10 seconds. Pass ctx.signal on to anything long-running. | Return null for values that are unknown, rather than 0. | Keep 2–5 blocks. A card is small. | .

562.title: 4. Optional: a custom look
562.content: Add client.js when blocks are not enough (a chart, a list, a progress bar). See the API reference. Render in the shadow root and use the theme variables.

563.title: 5. Add it to the dashboard
563.content: # settings.yaml plugins: - path: ./my-widgets/my-nas # relative to the config folder, or absolute . # services.yaml - Storage: - NAS: href: http://nas.lan:5000 widget: type: my-nas url: http://nas.lan:5000 key: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_NAS_KEY}}" . A path: widget is read again whenever a YAML file is saved: save settings.yaml after changing server.js and the open page shows the new version. A broken manifest or an unsupported apiVersion appears at the top of the page. A local widget with the same id as one in the widgets collection takes its place, which is how you try a change to a collection widget. npm run dev in the dashboard repository (with --config pointing at a test config) is handy while writing one.

564.title: 6. Test it
564.content: Test fetch without the dashboard by calling it with a fake ctx; the template’s tests show how. tests/installer.test.mjs in the dashboard repository tests the template end to end. Ready to share it? Make it a remote widget.

749.title: OpenWrt
749.content: type: openwrt · version 0.4.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . An OpenWrt router’s uptime and 5-minute load average, or with interfaceName (a device such as eth0 or br-lan) that interface’s state (marked when down) and the bytes sent and received, as homepage’s openwrt widget. The widget talks to ubus over /ubus, which needs a user with a read ACL. Create /usr/share/rpcd/acl.d/dashboard.json: . { "dashboard": { "description": "Dashboard", "read": { "ubus": { "network.device": ["status"], "system": ["info"] } } } } . make a password hash with uhttpd -m "<password>", and add the user to /etc/config/rpcd: . config login option username 'dashboard' option password '<the hash>' list read dashboard . then service rpcd restart. Learn more about OpenWrt.

827.title: Prometheus Metric
827.content: type: prometheusmetric · version 0.2.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . The results of up to four PromQL queries, each with your own label, as homepage’s prometheusmetric widget. Each entry of metrics has a label, a query (the first result of a vector, or a scalar, is shown) and optionally a key (for fields) and a format: . | type: text (default), number, percent, bytes, bits, byterate, bitrate, duration (seconds as a span), relativeDate (milliseconds, as a span from now) or date (milliseconds). homepage’s binary types (bbytes, bibyterate, …) show decimal units, as everywhere in this collection. | scale: a number, or a fraction such as 1/16, to multiply by. | prefix and suffix: text before and after the value. | options.maximumFractionDigits for number and percent. | . The widget refreshes every 10 seconds; set refreshInterval (milliseconds) on the entry for another rate. Fill in username and password when Prometheus sits behind basic authentication. Learn more about querying Prometheus.

828.title: Display fields
828.content: The blocks are the metrics you configure: fields takes their key (or label). Pick them with fields: in the entry.

829.title: Configuration options
829.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | E.g. http://prometheus.lan:9090 | . | metrics | list | yes |   | [{ label, query, key?, format: { type, scale, prefix, suffix, options } }] | . | username | string |   |   | When Prometheus sits behind basic authentication | . | password | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

830.title: Example
830.content: # services.yaml - Monitoring: - Prometheus: href: http://prometheus.lan:9090 icon: prometheus widget: type: prometheusmetric fields: [fields, key, label] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults url: http://prometheus.lan:9090 metrics: - label: Alerts query: count(ALERTS{alertstate="firing"}) or vector(0) - label: Disk free query: node_filesystem_avail_bytes{mountpoint="/"} format: { type: bytes } - label: Uptime query: time() - node_boot_time_seconds format: { type: duration } .

832.title: Providers
832.content: Many widgets need an API key, or a username and password. A provider is such an account, defined once under providers: in settings.yaml and used by every widget that needs it, as homepage’s providers: . # settings.yaml providers: radarr: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_RADARR_KEY}}" # a text: the key nas: # a map: the options it names url: https://nas.lan:5001 username: dashboard password: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_NAS_PASSWORD}}" . A widget uses one with provider: <name>: . # services.yaml - Media: - Radarr: href: http://radarr.lan:7878 widget: type: radarr url: http://radarr.lan:7878 provider: radarr # fills the key - Storage: - DiskStation: widget: type: diskstation provider: nas # fills url, username and password .

833.title: How a provider fills a widget
833.content: . | A text fills the widget’s first secret option that the entry leaves out: its key or token. | A map fills the options it names, such as url, username, password or key, again only those the entry leaves out. Options a widget does not have are skipped. | What the entry sets itself always wins, so one provider can serve widgets that differ in one option. | . A provider that does not exist is a config error on the widget, shown at the top of the page.

834.title: Keeping them secret
834.content: . | Nothing under providers: reaches the browser. Every value in it is a secret, also one written there literally; secret values are scrubbed from error messages too. | Use variables, not passwords: {{DASHBOARD_VAR_NAME}} takes the environment variable DASHBOARD_VAR_NAME, and {{DASHBOARD_FILE_NAME}} the contents of the file whose path is in DASHBOARD_FILE_NAME, such as a Docker secret (see Variables). settings.yaml then holds the names of the variables, not the passwords, and can be shared or kept in git. | . # compose.yaml of the dashboard services: dashboard: image: ghcr.io/stefanrenne/dashboard:latest environment: DASHBOARD_VAR_RADARR_KEY: 0123456789abcdef # or from an .env file next to compose.yaml DASHBOARD_FILE_NAS_PASSWORD: /run/secrets/nas_password secrets: [nas_password] secrets: nas_password: file: ./nas_password.txt . With DASHBOARD_FILE_NAS_PASSWORD, write "{{DASHBOARD_FILE_NAS_PASSWORD}}" in settings.yaml instead of the DASHBOARD_VAR_ form.

835.title: Discovered services
835.content: A discovered service takes a provider the same way, as the Docker label dashboard.widget.provider (or dashboard.widgets[1].provider for the second widget), or the Kubernetes annotation getdashboard.dev/widget.provider: . # compose.yaml labels: - dashboard.name=Radarr - dashboard.widget.type=radarr - dashboard.widget.url=http://radarr:7878 - dashboard.widget.provider=radarr .

843.title: Proxmox VE
843.content: type: proxmox · version 0.3.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . Running and total virtual machines and LXC containers (templates left out), and the CPU and memory in use over the online nodes, as homepage’s proxmox widget. node limits it to one node. For one VM or container on a service’s card, use the dashboard’s own proxmoxNode and proxmoxVMID instead. Make a read-only API token: Datacenter > Permissions > API Tokens > Add (with Privilege Separation checked), then Datacenter > Permissions > Add > API Token Permission with path /, that token and the role PVEAuditor. username is the token id (api@pam!dashboard), password the secret Proxmox shows once. Proxmox uses a self-signed certificate by default, so insecure is on, as in homepage; set insecure: false with a trusted certificate. Learn more about Proxmox VE.

The token’s secret | . | node | string |   |   | Only this node; default the whole cluster | . | insecure | boolean |   | true | Accept Proxmox’s self-signed certificate (as homepage does) | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

849.title: Proxmox
849.content: The settings page edits this file under Proxmox as a form; “Advanced edit” opens it as text under Advanced. proxmox.yaml lists Proxmox nodes, for proxmoxNode: and proxmoxVMID: on a service (as in homepage): the VM’s or container’s state as a label in the card’s corner, with CPU and memory on a click. pve: # the node name, as in proxmoxNode url: https://pve.lan:8006 token: api@pam!dashboard # an API token id secret: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_PROXMOX_SECRET}}" # its secret insecure: true # default: accept Proxmox's self-signed certificate . homepage’s older form, one url, token and secret at the top for every node, works too. Make the token under Datacenter > Permissions > API Tokens and give it the role PVEAuditor on /; see the Proxmox VM widget page. token and secret stay on the server. For a whole node or cluster on one card (VMs, containers, CPU, memory), use the Proxmox widget.

857.title: Proxmox VM
857.content: type: proxmoxvm · version 1.3.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . State, CPU and memory of one Proxmox VM (QEMU) or LXC container, as in homepage. This is the widget behind a service’s proxmoxNode: and proxmoxVMID: (with proxmoxType: lxc for a container): the state shows as a label in the card’s corner, and a click on it shows CPU and memory. The connection comes from proxmox.yaml (see Configuration), per node or one for every node. A paused VM is marked; a stopped one shows as down. Make a read-only API token in Proxmox: Datacenter > Permissions > API Tokens > Add (with Privilege Separation checked), then Datacenter > Permissions > Add > API Token Permission with path /, that token and the role PVEAuditor. token is the token id (user@pam!dashboard), secret the value Proxmox shows once. Proxmox uses a self-signed certificate by default, so insecure is on, as in homepage. Set insecure: false in proxmox.yaml when Proxmox has a trusted certificate. Learn more about Proxmox VE.

858.title: Display fields
858.content: status, cpu, mem . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

859.title: Configuration options

869.title: Publishing
869.content: CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) does the work. Changes go to develop; main only moves to develop for a release, and a release is a tag on main. | Event | What CI does | . | Pull request | Tests, an amd64 image build and a smoke test. Nothing is pushed. Into develop, the tests use the widgets collection’s develop branch, otherwise its newest release. | . | Push to develop | Tests (with the collection’s develop branch), then the image for amd64 and arm64, pushed as develop only (version develop-<sha>). A push that changes only docs/, scripts/, tests/, examples/ or Markdown runs the tests only. | . | Push to main | Tests and the image for amd64 and arm64: nothing is pushed. | . | Tag vX.Y.Z | The same, pushed as latest, X.Y.Z and X.Y, and a GitHub release with that version’s CHANGELOG section. The tagged commit must be on main, or nothing is published. | . | Run by hand on main | As a tag, for package.json’s version when it is not released yet: CI creates the tag vX.Y.Z with the release. For when a tag cannot be pushed. | . | Run by hand on develop | As a push to develop (Dependabot’s auto-merge starts these). | . | Monday 04:23 UTC | Rebuild of the newest release (latest, X.Y.Z, X.Y), so base image security fixes arrive without a code change. | . A new push to a branch or a pull request cancels the older CI run of that branch or PR, which is still running. Runs for a tag, by hand and on the schedule are never cancelled.

870.title: Develop builds
870.content: ghcr.io/stefanrenne/dashboard:develop is the newest build of develop, to try what comes next; latest and the version tags stay on releases. A develop build reports develop-<sha> as its version (the footer links that commit) and installs the widgets collection from its develop branch instead of #latest, checked for new commits every pluginUpdateInterval (an hour by default). An entry for the collection in settings.yaml plugins: still wins. Going back to latest installs the collection’s newest release again.

871.title: Release steps
871.content: On develop, with everything for the release merged: . | Make sure CHANGELOG.md has everything under ## [Unreleased]. | Choose the version (semver) and set it in package.json (npm version <x.y.z> --no-git-tag-version). | Rename ## [Unreleased] to ## [x.y.z] - YYYY-MM-DD and add a fresh empty ## [Unreleased] above it. | Commit on develop and push it. | Move main to it: git push origin develop:main (a fast-forward; main never gets commits of its own, so this cannot fail unless someone pushed to main). | Tag that commit and push the tag: git tag -a vx.y.z -m vx.y.z, git push origin vx.y.z. CI fails the release when the CHANGELOG has no section for the version, or the tag is not on main. Without a tag push: run the CI workflow by hand on main (Actions > CI > Run workflow). | . A release of the widgets collection goes the same way (its develop, then main, then the tag). A change to the widget API is a release note of its own: say which apiVersion it belongs to.

872.title: Documentation site
872.content: getdashboard.dev is built from docs/ here, and published by a repository of its own, dashboard-site: its workflow site.yml builds the site and commits it to its gh-pages branch, which GitHub Pages serves (the domain is set there). It has two versions, with a menu in the header to switch (docs/_includes/header_custom.html): the release at the root, and develop under /develop/, with a banner on its pages, its widget pages from the collection’s develop, and robots.txt keeping it out of search engines. The menu opens the same page in the other version, or its home page when that page is not there.github/workflows/site.yml here starts that workflow (with a fine-grained token in the secret PAGES_DISPATCH_TOKEN, Actions read and write on dashboard-site; without it, it only says so): . | a push to develop: /develop/ is built again; | a push to main (a release): /develop/ is built again and copied to the root (scripts/pages-promote.sh), and /version.json gets the release’s version for the menu. No page is built for the release itself: what was on /develop/ is what is released; | a release of the widgets collection (its release job, with the same secret): the root is built from main’s docs with the collection at that release, and copied to the root the same way. | . A copy works because nothing on a page depends on the version it was built for, apart from what Jekyll writes for the base path: the menu and the banner read the version from the address, and pages-promote.sh points the base path (links, assets, the search index, canonical and redirect addresses) and the links to the develop branch at the root and main. So a page never links to develop’s address of the site itself (tests/pages.test.mjs checks). Jekyll builds it with the just-the-docs theme; the Markdown stays plain (no front matter), titles, the menu order and redirects from old addresses are in docs/_config.yml. The menu has four parts: Home (docs/README.md), Configuration (docs/configuration/, a page per file as in homepage), Widgets and Extend (docs/extend/). scripts/pages.sh stages one version (DOCS_CHANNEL=develop gives baseurl: /develop and GitHub links at develop): it points links outside docs/ at GitHub and wraps each page in {% raw %} so {{DASHBOARD_VAR_*}} examples stay literal. scripts/widget-images.mjs then photographs the widgets with example data, and scripts/pages-widgets.mjs adds a page per widget from its README.md and widget.yaml (with that image), split into service and header widgets, and the list of all of them on the Widgets page. Only a widget whose hash changed is photographed again: its folder in the collection, the collection’s mock, and what draws it here (RENDER_FILES in the script). The published images, with their <id>.hash files, are the cache (DOCS_IMAGE_CACHE); when every hash matches, Playwright does not even start. scripts/check-highlight.rb then runs every code block through Rouge, at the version GitHub Pages uses, and fails the build on one it would mark red (tests/pages.test.mjs catches the known cases locally, without Ruby). Widget pages stay at widgets/collection/<id>.html, whatever their section: other sites link there. A new page gets an entry under defaults: in docs/_config.yml; a moved page a redirect_from with its old address.

873.title: Dependabot
873.content: .github/dependabot.yml opens grouped weekly PRs for GitHub Actions, npm and the Docker base image, into develop: they ship with the next release. The Node major in the image is kept on an LTS line by hand (Dependabot ignores Node majors). dependabot-automerge.yml merges them when CI passes and builds develop. A PR that changes a workflow file needs a fine-grained token in the repository secret AUTOMERGE_TOKEN (Contents, Pull requests and Workflows: read and write); without it those PRs wait for a manual merge.
