917.title: A remote widget
917.content: A remote widget lives in a git repository or an npm package. Users add it with one line under plugins:; the dashboard downloads it, pins the version in plugins/plugins.lock.yaml and runs it. The widget is written as a local one; this page is about the repository around it.

918.title: 1. Start from the example repository
918.content: Start from dashboard-widget-example (Use this template on GitHub): the same widget as examples/widget-template, set up as a repository with tests that run without the dashboard and CI that releases a version tag, so users can install it with #latest. Then give it your widget’s id: . npm run rename -- my-nas --name "My NAS" . That renames example-counter everywhere: the id and name in widget.yaml, the dash-<id> element in client.js, name in package.json (dashboard-widget-<id>), the README and the tests. While you write it, point a test dashboard at your clone with path: (see a local widget).

919.title: 2. Document it
919.content: Give the widget a README.md in its folder, in the format of the widgets collection, so users find the same things in the same place: . | # <name>, as in widget.yaml. | What it shows, and what the user must set up in the service: where the API key is, which ids to fill in, when an option is only needed with authentication on. | ## Fields: every block key, so users know what to put in fields:. | ## Example: a complete services.yaml entry, with the key through {{DASHBOARD_VAR_...}}. | . Give each option in widget.yaml a line comment when its name does not explain it (url: { type: url, required: true } # e.g. http://radarr:7878).

920.title: 3. Publish
920.content: . | git: push, tag v1.0.0 (match version in widget.yaml). The example repository’s CI makes a GitHub release of each tag. | npm: npm publish (add the keyword dashboard-widget). A package with a package.json needs "type": "module". | . Bump version on every release; the dashboard installs each version in its own folder.

921.title: 4. Get listed
921.content: Add a row to the Catalogue with a pull request on the dashboard repository (docs/widgets/catalogue.md, in alphabetical order). A package is listed when it: . | is public: a git repository with release tags, or an npm package; | targets the current widget API (apiVersion: 2 in its widget.yaml); | has a README as in 2. Document it; | keeps keys and passwords in secret: true options, and marks options that run something or reach elsewhere discoverable: false (see the API reference). | . A listing says the package exists, not that it was reviewed.

922.title: 5. How users install it
922.content: # settings.yaml plugins: - source: git+https://github.com/you/dashboard-widget-my-nas#v1.0.0 # a tag, a branch or a 40-character commit - source: git+https://github.com/you/dashboard-widget-my-nas#latest # the newest release tag, checked hourly - source: npm:dashboard-widget-my-nas@1.0.0 - source: git+https://github.com/you/widgets#v3.0.0 subdir: widgets/my-nas # one widget of a repository with several - source: git+https://github.com/you/widgets#v3.0.0 only: [my-nas, my-router] # a collection: only these folders . A repository without widget.yaml at its root is a collection: every folder with a widget.yaml directly in it, or in its widgets/ folder, is installed. See Plugins for updates, the lock file and pluginUpdateInterval. Users run your code on their server: see Security for what a widget can reach and what to tell your users.

924.title: System resources
924.content: type: resources · version 1.6.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . CPU, memory, disk, CPU temperature, uptime and network as meters, like homepage’s resources widget. It measures the machine (or container) the dashboard runs on: in Docker, mount a host folder to see that disk, for example -v /mnt/data:/mnt/data:ro. Meters turn amber from 85% and red from 95%. Everything is off by default; turn on what you want to see. cputemp and network read Linux’s /sys: the temperature is the highest thermal zone, network: true follows the default route (or name an interface, network: eno1; in Docker mount /sys:/sys:ro for a host interface). expanded: true adds used / total under memory and disk, and the CPU load.

925.content: cpu, memory, disk (with one mount point), or one per mount point named after it (/, /mnt/data), cputemp, uptime, rx, tx . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

926.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | cpu | boolean |   | false |   | . | memory | boolean |   | false |   | . | disk | list |   | [] | Mount points, e.g. [”/”, “/media”], or one as text | . | cputemp | boolean |   | false | The highest thermal zone (Linux) | . | tempmin | number |   |   | Bottom of the temperature bar (default 0 °C / 32 °F) | . | tempmax | number |   |   | Top of the temperature bar (default 100 °C / 212 °F) | . | units | metric / imperial |   | metric | For the CPU temperature | . | uptime | boolean |   | false |   | . | network | string |   |   | True for the default interface, or a name such as eno1 (Linux) | . | diskUnits | bytes / bbytes |   | bytes | Bbytes: KiB, MiB, GiB (1024) | . | expanded | boolean |   | false | Also used / total, and the CPU load | . | label | string |   |   | Shown under the meters, e.g. “Media” | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

927.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | memory | number | Memory in use, in % | . | disk | number | Disk in use, in % | . | attention | boolean | True while the card marks something as needing attention | .

954.content: type: search · version 1.6.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . A search box. 959.title: Trust model
959.content: A widget’s server.js runs with the dashboard’s rights: network, files in the container, environment variables. Installing a widget means trusting its author, like choosing a Docker image. The dashboard limits the damage where it can: . | Plugins come only from sources listed in settings.yaml, plus the project’s own widgets collection (#latest), which is always installed. The page cannot add a source; POST /api/plugins/sync only re-reads the config. | Sources are pinned. A git tag or commit, #latest (the newest release tag at install time), or an exact npm version, is recommended; a branch or range gives a warning. plugins/plugins.lock.yaml records the commit or the npm tarball integrity, so a restart installs exactly the same code without network access. A changed npm tarball for a locked version is refused. | npm pack runs with --ignore-scripts; nothing from a package runs during installation. | git, npm and ping get validated arguments without a shell (no --prefixed refs or names). | The default collection yields: a widget id from your own plugins: wins over the collection’s, and two of your own sources cannot share an id. | Host names are checked (allowedHosts in settings.yaml, see Allowed hosts): a web page that points a name of its own at your network (DNS rebinding) gets a refusal instead of the dashboard, so it cannot read it or press its buttons through your browser. * turns this off. | Actions run for anyone who can open the page, unless they ask for a password. Without a login: a widget with an action (the collection’s button running a script) does its thing for every visitor who presses it. With an admin password (settings.yaml adminPassword, a scrypt hash), root buttons, webhooks, the widget sync and every entry with confirm: password or always ask for it first (see Admin password); a correct one unlocks that browser for a while through an HttpOnly cookie the server keeps in memory, and guessing is slowed down per address. A passkey (see Passkeys) counts as the password: over HTTPS only, bound to the host name it was made on, with user verification, its challenge used once and a one-time token for the request that follows. | The settings page writes settings.yaml. It opens only with the admin password (or a login); a new admin password needs the current one, and only its hash is written. Without an admin password yet, it answers only the local network, and only to set one. Its endpoints read a JSON body (at most 64 KB) and need X-Requested-With: dashboard. | login: true closes the page itself (see Login page): every request needs a session, which the server keeps in .sessions.json (hashes of the tokens, mode 600) and checks each time; a logout or a new admin password ends it for good. Only /api/health, robots.txt and the login page stay open. Without it, anyone who can open the page reads it: put the dashboard behind your proxy’s authentication (see Authentication in front), or keep such buttons off a dashboard that is reachable from outside. Only the configured script or command runs; nothing in the request reaches it. | Root scripts are off unless you ask for them. Only with DASHBOARD_ALLOW_ROOT_SCRIPTS=true on the container does the image let node run /usr/local/bin/dashboard-root (bash as root) through sudo, for a button with user: root. Then every widget could, so a plugin you install can be root in the container too. A mounted Docker socket already gives that much: whoever can use the socket can start a root container. | The dashboard, and so every widget, runs as the unprivileged node user. The entrypoint is root only to give node a mounted Docker socket’s group, before the dashboard starts. | The setup wizard of a first install writes the config folder, lists the containers and runs a widget once to test it. It exists only while /config/.onboarding is there (an empty folder at the first start); every other request to it is a 404. It answers a visitor whose address, and every address a proxy passed on, is private; anyone else needs the code from the log (wrong ones are slowed down per address), and what it changes needs X-Requested-With: dashboard. Its endpoints are the only ones that read a request body: JSON only, at most 1 MB. It never overwrites a file that is there. | A mounted Docker socket gives every widget the whole Docker API (:ro does not limit it). Use a docker-socket-proxy with CONTAINERS=1 when you install widgets you do not fully trust. | Installed widgets’ server.js runs in a worker thread with a memory limit (DASHBOARD_WIDGET_MEMORY_MB, default 256): a widget stuck in a loop or eating memory stops the worker, which starts again, not the dashboard. A worker thread is not a security boundary: it has the same network and files (the config folder too). Its environment leaves out the DASHBOARD_VAR_* / DASHBOARD_FILE_* variables, so a widget reads only the values its options get. DASHBOARD_WIDGET_ISOLATION=off runs installed widgets in the dashboard process, as before. | Labels and annotations are not config. Whoever starts a container (or builds its image) writes its labels, so discovered services cannot use variables unless allowVariables lists them, nor set options marked discoverable: false, framed options, provider, references to other services or target: hidden-iframe (see What labels may do). Mark an option discoverable: false when it runs something or reaches elsewhere with the dashboard’s rights. | .

960.title: Secrets
960.content: . | Options marked secret: true, undeclared options, and every value from {{DASHBOARD_VAR_*}} / {{DASHBOARD_FILE_*}} stay on the server. /api/layout contains public options only (tested). | Error messages from widgets and config messages have secret values replaced by ***. | The settings page shows the config files with their secrets as tokens (__SECRET_…__): options marked secret: true, providers, adminPassword and Proxmox secrets written in the file itself. A save puts the values back on the server; {{DASHBOARD_VAR_*}} placeholders are shown as written, never filled in. The admin password is not changed through a file, only with the current one. | The page’s Content-Security-Policy restricts connect-src to the dashboard itself, and scripts to files it serves: the page’s own inline script carries a nonce that changes with every load, so an inline script or event handler that got into the page anyway does not run. | A widget’s client.js (and custom.js) runs in the page itself, by design: it can do what the page does (read /api/layout, call the endpoints with the page’s header, change other cards). Installing a widget trusts its client as much as its server. | .

961.title: Recommendations for users
961.content: . | Prefer widgets whose source you can read; pin tags or commits. | Put secrets in variables (DASHBOARD_VAR_*) or files (DASHBOARD_FILE_*, e.g. Docker secrets), not in the YAML. | Do not expose the dashboard to the internet without authentication: its login page, or a proxy with single sign-on in front (see Authentication in front). | Give Docker access through a socket proxy that only allows reading containers. | .

969.title: Services
969.content: services.yaml holds the cards: groups of services, each with a link, an icon, a status check and any number of widgets. Services can also be discovered from Docker labels and Kubernetes annotations. - Group name: - Service name: href: http://app.lan # link of the card icon: app.svg # dashboard-icons name (.svg/.png/.webp), /icons/..., or a URL description: One line statusStyle: dot # overrides settings.statusStyle for this service showStats: true # overrides settings.showStats for this service weight: 50 # order within the group, low first; default (position + 1) x 100 filter: widget.update == false # hide the card while this is true (see Filters) target: _self # overrides settings.target; hidden-iframe: the dashboard # server calls the URL (a webhook) and shows how it went confirm: none # a hidden-iframe webhook asks for the admin password; none: it does not # (also on a widget entry: password, always or none; see Admin password) # status check, the first one that is set: siteMonitor: http://app.lan # HTTP check (http-status widget) ping: app.lan # ICMP ping (ping widget) container: app # Docker container state (docker widget) server: local # which docker.yaml server; optional with one server proxmoxNode: pve # Proxmox VM or container state (proxmoxvm widget, proxmox.yaml) proxmoxVMID: 101 proxmoxType: qemu # qemu (a VM, default) or lxc (a container) app: app # Kubernetes: the pods labelled app.kubernetes.io/name=app (kubernetes-pods widget) namespace: apps # their namespace (default: default) podSelector: tier=web # another label selector instead of app's external: true # no pod status for this app # widgets: widget: type: custom-api url: http://app.lan/api mappings: [{ field: users, label: Users }] widgets: # or several - type: ping host: app.lan refreshInterval: 5000 # dashboard keys, for every widget: refreshInterval (ms) or fields: [latency] # refresh (5s), fields (which blocks), hide_errors . Nested groups, as in homepage: an entry whose value is a list (instead of a map) is a group inside the group. Its layout goes inside the parent’s layout in settings.yaml, and it is on the parent’s tab. # services.yaml - Infrastructure: - Router: href: http://router.lan - Network: # a nested group - Access point: href: http://ap.lan - Switch: href: http://switch.lan . # settings.yaml layout: Infrastructure: style: row Network: # the nested group's layout columns: 2 . Block highlighting, as in homepage: highlight: on a widget entry colours blocks by their value. Keys are block keys (the names fields: uses). The first matching rule wins; numeric rules are tried before string rules. widget: type: sonarr url: http://sonarr.lan:8989 key: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_SONARR_KEY}}" highlight: queued: valueOnly: true # colour the value only, not the whole block numeric: - { level: danger, when: gte, value: 20 } - { level: warn, when: between, min: 5, max: 19 } - { level: good, when: eq, value: 0 } status: string: - { level: danger, when: regex, value: "(failed|import) pending" } . Numeric when: gt, gte, lt, lte, eq, ne (with value), between and outside (with min and/or max); numbers are read from formatted values such as 1,234 GB. String when: equals, includes, startsWith, endsWith (case-insensitive unless caseSensitive: true) and regex (flags, default i). Every rule takes negate: true. The colours per level can be changed in settings.yaml with homepage’s Tailwind classes; colours outside the dashboard’s palettes are ignored: . blockHighlights: levels: good: "bg-emerald-500/40 text-emerald-950 dark:bg-emerald-900/60 dark:text-emerald-400" warn: "bg-amber-300/30 text-amber-900 dark:bg-amber-900/30 dark:text-amber-200" danger: "bg-rose-700/45 text-rose-200 dark:bg-rose-950/70 dark:text-rose-400" . Every check that is set gets its own label in the card’s top-right corner, as in homepage: the response time (or “down”) for siteMonitor and ping, the container state for container. Click a container label to see the container’s CPU and memory. ping also accepts a URL (ping: http://192.168.1.2). Icons: a dashboard-icons name, an mdi-, si- or sh- icon, a file in config/icons or a URL; see Images. The settings page edits this file under Services as a form; “Advanced edit” opens it as text under Advanced.

970.title: Filtering services
970.content: filter: on a service hides its card while an expression is true, such as filter: widget.update == false or filter: ping.attention; on one of its widgets it hides that widget. See Filters.

972.title: Settings
972.content: settings.yaml holds everything about the page itself: title, language, look, the order and layout of the groups, and the widget packages to install. Every key is optional. title: Homelab description: The start page of my homelab # meta description, for link previews and search engines favicon: /icons/lab.svg # a URL, a dashboard-icons name (proxmox.svg) or a file in config/icons; default: dashboard.svg startUrl: / # where the installed app opens pwa: # installing the dashboard as an app (site.webmanifest) icons: # without icons, the favicon is the app icon - { src: /icons/app-192.png, sizes: 192x192, type: image/png } - { src: /icons/app-512.png, sizes: 512x512, type: image/png } shortcuts: # long-press menu of the app icon - { name: Media, url: "/#media", description: The media group } language: en # en, nl, fr, de, es, ca, he, hr, hu, it, nb-NO, pt, ru, sv, vi, zh-Hans, zh-Hant (zh-CN works too) theme: auto # auto, dark, light color: slate # a Tailwind colour: slate, gray, zinc, neutral, stone, red, orange, amber, yellow, lime, # green, emerald, teal, cyan, sky, blue, indigo, violet, purple, fuchsia, pink, rose showTitle: true # false: the title is only the browser tab title (as in homepage) headerStyle: boxed # boxed, clean, underlined (a line under the header) or boxedWidgets (a box per widget) cardStyle: hairline # a thin border instead of the shadow blockStyle: refined # heavier, larger values in widget blocks font: plexData # IBM Plex Mono for values, the clock and status labels; plex: for everything quicklaunch: # start typing anywhere on the page to find a service, bookmark or web search searchDescriptions: true # also match descriptions (name matches come first) provider: duckduckgo # google, duckduckgo, bing, baidu, brave, startpage or custom (+ url); # default: the search widget's provider; none: no web search # url: https://search.lan/?q= # for custom: the query is appended, or put where {q} is target: _blank # where the web search opens showSearchSuggestions: true # suggestions from the search engine (default: the search widget's setting) # suggestionUrl: https://ac.search.lan/?q= # for custom: an OpenSearch suggestion URL hideInternetSearch: false # true: no web search entry hideVisitURL: false # true: no "open <url>" entry for typed addresses mobileButtonPosition: bottom-right # a search button on phones: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right providers: # shared keys and logins (see Providers); a widget entry uses one with provider: <name> openweathermap: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_OWM_KEY}}" # a text fills the widget's first secret option left empty (its key) longhorn: # a map fills the options it names url: https://longhorn.lan username: admin password: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_LONGHORN_PASSWORD}}" instanceName: internal # for discovery labels meant for one dashboard (dashboard.instance.internal.href) hideVersion: true # hide the versions in the footer (shown by default, as in homepage): # `core v0.7.3 | widgets v0.4.1`, each linking to its release or commit pluginUpdateInterval: 1h # how often #latest and branch plugins are checked for a newer version (false: never) allowedHosts: [dash.lan] # the names you open the dashboard by (IP addresses always work); see Allowed hosts adminPassword: "scrypt:16384:8:1:..." # the admin password's hash (node src/hash-password.mjs); see Admin password login: true # a login page with the admin password ({ remember: 7d }); see Login page actions: remember: 15m # a correct admin password unlocks the browser this long (0: ask every press) disableUpdateCheck: true # do not ask GitHub once a day for a newer release (only asked while the version is shown) disableIndexing: true # ask search engines not to index the page (robots.txt and a robots meta tag) base: https://lab.example.com/dashboard/ # behind a reverse proxy under a sub path: the page's address logpath: /config # also log to <logpath>/logs/dashboard.log, rotated at 10 MiB, five files kept; # without it the log goes to stdout only. LOG_TARGETS (env): both, stdout or file showStats: true # container stats open from the start instead of on a click; a service can set its own statusStyle: dot # status labels: dot (a coloured dot) or basic (Online/Offline for siteMonitor and ping); # default: the response time and container state. A service can set its own. target: _blank # default link target of services background: https://example.com/wallpaper.jpg # optional; or a map, as in homepage: # background: # image: https://example.com/wallpaper.jpg # blur: sm # xs, sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl, 3xl # saturate: 50 # 0-200 (%) # brightness: 75 # 0-200 (%) # opacity: 50 # 0-100 (%) cardBlur: md # frosted cards over the background: xs, sm, md, lg, xl, 2xl, 3xl bookmarksStyle: icons # every bookmark group as icons only (a group can set iconsOnly: false) iconStyle: gradient # mdi- and si- icons: gradient (default) or theme (flat, in the theme colour) fullWidth: true # use the whole window width (default: at most 1280px) maxGroupColumns: 6 # groups side by side on wide screens (1536px and up), up to 8 maxBookmarkGroupColumns: 8 # the same for bookmark groups useEqualHeights: true # cards in a row equally high; a group can override it disableCollapse: true # group titles are plain titles, not fold buttons groupsInitiallyCollapsed: true # every group starts folded; a group's initiallyCollapsed wins layout: Media: columns: 3 # cards per row (2 on tablets, 1 on phones); the group spans the full width header: false # hide the group title initiallyCollapsed: true # start folded; viewers fold and unfold groups by clicking the title icon: plex.svg # category icon before the title: an icon name, /icons/..., or a URL useEqualHeights: false # overrides the global setting for this group Developer: # a bookmark group iconsOnly: true # only the icons, the name as tooltip Tools: style: column # default without columns: groups side by side, cards stacked discovery: interval: 30s plugins: - source: git+https://github.com/someone/dashboard-widget-x#v1.0.0 # tag, branch or 40-char commit - source: git+https://github.com/someone/dashboard-widget-v#latest # the newest release tag - source: npm:dashboard-widget-y@2.0.1 - source: git+https://github.com/someone/widgets#v3.0.0 subdir: widgets/z # a repo with several widgets - path: ./my-widgets/w # relative to the config folder - source: git+https://github.com/someone/widgets#v1.0.0 # a collection: every widget in it, only: [radarr, sonarr] # or only these folders .

973.title: Plugins
973.content: The settings page edits this list under Widgets, and installs again or updates from there. The widgets collection is always installed, as git+https://github.com/stefanrenne/dashboard-widgets#latest; the entries under plugins: extend it. To pin it or take only some of its widgets, list that repository yourself (with a tag, only: or subdir:): your entry then takes its place. A widget of your own with the same id as one in the collection (for example a local checkout under path:) wins. Every widget comes from the collection, also the ones behind a service’s siteMonitor: (http-status), ping: (ping), container: (docker), app: (kubernetes-pods) and proxmoxNode: (proxmoxvm). An only: list for the collection always gets those five added, so the service fields keep working. An entry pinned to a release too old for them says so in the messages. The first start downloads the collection, so it needs network access once; after that the lock file keeps it without network. #latest installs the highest release tag (v1.2.3 or 1.2.3; pre-releases such as v2.0.0-beta.1 are skipped) and records it in plugins/plugins.lock.yaml. A restart keeps that release; POST /api/plugins/sync?update=1 (or deleting its entry from the lock file) moves it to the newest release. The folder of the previous version is then deleted. An update that fails (offline, a broken release) keeps the version that worked and says so in the messages. A branch named latest can no longer be used as #latest. The widgets collection is the exception: when its #latest is locked at a release older than the one this dashboard needs (0.4.0 for 0.6), the next start moves it to the newest release by itself. pluginUpdateInterval (default 1h, at least 1m, false turns it off) is how often the sources that can move (#latest, a branch) are asked for a newer version: one git ls-remote each, nothing is downloaded. Only a newer version is installed, which reloads the open pages; pinned tags and commits are never asked. plugins.lock.yaml then records the new version. The widgets collection is the exception: when its #latest is locked at a release older than the one this dashboard needs (0.4.0 for 0.6), the next start moves it to the newest release by itself. A source without widget.yaml at its root is a collection: every folder with a widget.yaml directly in it, or in its widgets/ folder, is installed.

974.title: Layout
974.content: The settings page edits this block under Groups, keeping its form (a map or a list) and its comments. Order, as in homepage: groups appear in the order of the layout block, discovered groups too; groups that are not in it follow, in their own order. Service and bookmark groups can be mixed: a bookmark group listed between service groups is shown there. The layout block can also be a list, which reads more naturally when it is only about the order: . layout: - Media: - Developer: # a bookmark group, shown between Media and Infrastructure - Infrastructure: style: row . Tabs, as in homepage: give layout groups a tab and the page shows a tab bar. Service and bookmark groups without a tab show on every tab. Each tab has its own address: # plus its name in lowercase (http://dashboard.lan/#media). tabs: sets their order, an icon per tab and the tab that opens first, and header widgets can be on a tab too: see Tabs. layout: Infrastructure: tab: Home Developer: # a bookmark group tab: Home Media: tab: Media Tools: # no tab: on every tab style: row . Viewers can pick light, dark or “follow the system” and another colour with the buttons in the footer; that choice is remembered in their browser and overrides theme and color. To write a widget package of your own, see Extend.

976.title: Shelly
976.content: type: shelly · version 1.2.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . A Shelly device’s firmware version and, when a newer one is available, that version in a block marked as needing attention, with an Update firmware button under the blocks that starts it. An up-to-date device shows only its version. While the device updates, the button says the update started; it goes away once the device reports the new version. Works with Gen2, Gen3 and Gen4 devices (the RPC API) and with Gen1 devices. Set password only when the device has authentication on (Settings > Authentication on Gen2 and newer, Internet & Security > Restrict login on Gen1): Gen2 and newer log in as admin with digest authentication, Gen1 with the username and password set there. When the device refuses the password, or asks for one while none is set, the card says so. Fill the password in through {{DASHBOARD_VAR_...}}, not {{...}} alone: an unknown placeholder stays literal and is refused. The widget asks the device to look for new firmware at most once an hour (it also looks by itself); with beta: true a beta version is offered when there is no newer stable one. Anyone who can open the dashboard can press the button: put the dashboard behind authentication before you add it. The device restarts at the end of the update, so the card shows an error for a moment. Learn more about Shelly.

977.content: firmware, update (only when an update is available or being installed) . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

Only when the device has authentication on | . | username | string |   | admin | Gen1 only; Gen2 and newer always use admin | . | beta | boolean |   | false | Also offer beta firmware | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

979.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | update | boolean | True while an update is available or being installed | . | version | string | The installed firmware | . | available | string | The firmware on offer, or null | .

1054.title: Tabs
1054.content: The settings page edits tabs under Tabs; a group’s tab is chosen under Groups and a header widget’s under Header widgets. Tabs split the dashboard into pages: a tab bar under the header, and each tab shows its own groups and header widgets. Groups and header widgets without a tab are on every tab, so a search box or a group of tools can stay put while the rest changes. Each tab has its own address: # and its name in lowercase, with spaces as %20 (http://dashboard.lan/#media, http://dashboard.lan/#home%20lab). Use it for a bookmark, a browser start page, startUrl or a PWA shortcut. Without a #, the page opens on the tab marked default, or else on the first one.

1055.title: The tabs
1055.content: tabs: in settings.yaml lists the tabs in the order of the tab bar. A tab is just its name, or a map with a name, an icon and default: . tabs: - Home - name: Media icon: mdi-play-circle # any icon a service takes: mdi-, si-, sh-, dashboard-icons, /icons/... default: true # opens without a # in the address (one tab) - name: Lab icon: proxmox.svg . tabs: is optional. A tab a group names (see below) is a tab too: those that tabs: does not list follow it, in the order of the layout block. homepage’s configuration, which has no tabs:, keeps working as it is.

1056.title: Groups on a tab
1056.content: A group gets its tab in the layout block of settings.yaml, as in homepage. This works for service groups and bookmark groups alike. A nested group is on its parent’s tab. layout: Infrastructure: tab: Lab Media: tab: Media Developer: # a bookmark group tab: Home Tools: # no tab: on every tab style: row . Discovered groups . A container or Ingress can put its group on a tab with the tab label (Docker) or annotation (Kubernetes). It is used when the layout block gives that group no tab; when two services of one group name different tabs, the first one counts and the other gets a warning. labels: dashboard.name: Jellyfin dashboard.group: Media dashboard.tab: Media . annotations: getdashboard.dev/enabled: "true" getdashboard.dev/group: Monitoring getdashboard.dev/tab: Lab .

1057.title: Header widgets on a tab
1057.content: A widget in widgets.yaml takes tab: with a tab name, or a list of them for several tabs. Without it, it is on every tab. The header box is left out on a tab without any header widget. - datetime: dateStyle: long # every tab - resources: cpu: true memory: true tab: Lab - openmeteo: latitude: 52.37 longitude: 4.89 tab: [Home, Media] . A name that is no tab gives a warning; a widget whose names are all unknown is shown on every tab. A widget that declares an option called tab itself gets the value as its own option.

1058.title: On the settings page
1058.content: Under Tabs you add, rename, reorder and remove tabs, give them an icon and choose the one that opens first. Saving writes tabs: only when it is needed (an icon, a default, an order of its own, or a tab no group names yet). | Renaming a tab moves its groups and header widgets with it: settings.yaml and widgets.yaml are both updated. | Removing a tab puts its groups and header widgets on every tab. | . The Tab field of a group (under Groups) and the Shown on boxes of a header widget (under Header widgets) choose from these tabs.

1059.title: Refreshing
1059.content: Widgets on a tab that is not shown do not ask for data. They ask as soon as their tab opens, and from then on at their normal interval.

Times show as spans (“2d 3h”). Make an API access token on the keys page (it expires after at most 90 days). 1133.title: UniFi Controller
1133.content: type: unifi (or unifi_console) · version 0.4.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . Uptime, WAN status and the users and devices on LAN and WLAN, from a UniFi Network controller (UniFi OS consoles such as the Dream Machine and Cloud Key, or a self-hosted controller). Without fields it shows uptime, WAN, LAN users and WLAN users, as in homepage; subsystems the controller does not report (no gateway, no access points) are left out, and a subsystem that is down is marked. Sign in with either: . | an API key (UniFi OS 4 and later): Settings › Control Plane › Integrations, put it in key; | or a local account with read access (not a UI.com cloud account): username and password. The widget tries UniFi OS first and falls back to a classic controller. | . site is the site’s name or description as the controller shows it; without it, the default site. Most controllers use a self-signed certificate: set insecure: true to accept it (the connection stays encrypted, but the certificate is not checked). In widgets.yaml the header form also works under homepage’s name, unifi_console. Learn more about UniFi Network.

1134.title: Display fields
1134.content: uptime, wan, lan, lan_users, lan_devices, wlan, wlan_users, wlan_devices . Pick them with fields: in the entry; without it the widget shows uptime, wan, lan_users, wlan_users.

An API key (UniFi OS: Settings > Control Plane > Integrations), or: | . | username | string |   |   | A local account with read access | . | password | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. | . | insecure | boolean |   | false | True: accept the controller’s self-signed certificate | . 1157.title: UptimeRobot
1157.content: type: uptimerobot · version 0.4.0 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . With a Read-Only API Key the monitors that are up and down (marked) in your UptimeRobot account; with a Monitor-Specific API Key that monitor’s state (down marked), how long it has been up, and how long ago and for how long it was last down, as homepage’s uptimerobot widget. Both keys are under My Settings > API Settings. Learn more about UptimeRobot.

1158.title: Display fields
1158.content: sitesUp, sitesDown, status, uptime, lastDown, downDuration . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

1159.title: Configuration options
1159.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | key | string | yes |   | Secret: stays on the server. My Settings > API: a Read-Only or a Monitor-Specific API Key | . | url | url |   | https://api.uptimerobot.com |   | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

1160.title: Filter attributes
1160.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | status | string | The monitor’s state: up, seemsdown, down, paused or notyetchecked | . | uptimeHours | number | Hours the monitor is up; null while it is not up, and with a key for several monitors | . | hoursSinceDown | number | Hours since the monitor last went down; null when it never did | . | attention | boolean | True while the card marks something as needing attention | .

1161.title: Example
1161.content: # services.yaml - Monitoring: - UptimeRobot: href: https://dashboard.uptimerobot.com icon: uptimerobot widget: type: uptimerobot fields: [sitesUp, sitesDown, status, uptime, lastDown, downDuration] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults key: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_UPTIMEROBOT_KEY}}" .

1163.title: UrBackup
1163.content: type: urbackup · version 0.3.2 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . The clients whose backups are fine, failed (marked) or not recent (marked), and with fields the space all backups take, as homepage’s urbackup widget. A client is fine when its file backup, and its image backup when it makes those, ran within maxDays (default 3) without errors. The widget logs in with a user of UrBackup’s web interface (or anonymously without one); it sees the clients that user may see. Learn more about UrBackup.

1164.title: Display fields
1164.content: ok, errored, noRecent, totalUsed . Pick them with fields: in the entry; without it the widget shows ok, errored, noRecent.

1165.title: Configuration options
1165.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | The web interface, e.g. http://urbackup.lan:55414 | . | username | string |   |   | Without one the anonymous login is used | . | password | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. | . | maxDays | number |   | 3 | Days after which a client’s last backup is not recent | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

1166.title: Filter attributes
1166.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | ok | number | Clients whose backups are recent and without errors | . | errored | number | Clients whose last backup failed | . | noRecent | number | Clients without a recent backup | . | attention | boolean | True while the card marks something as needing attention | .

1167.title: Example
1167.content: # services.yaml - Backups: - UrBackup: href: http://urbackup.lan:55414 icon: urbackup widget: type: urbackup fields: [ok, errored, noRecent, totalUsed] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults url: http://urbackup.lan:55414 username: dashboard password: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_URBACKUP_PASSWORD}}" maxDays: 5 .

1169.title: Vikunja
1169.content: type: vikunja · version 0.3.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . Your projects in Vikunja and the open tasks due within a week, overdue (marked) and in progress, as homepage’s vikunja widget. enableTaskList: true adds the next five tasks by due date as rows. Create a token under Settings > API Tokens with read access to projects and tasks, and use it as key. For Vikunja 1.0.0-rc4 and later set version: 2. Learn more about Vikunja.

1170.title: Display fields
1170.content: projects, tasks7d, tasksOverdue, tasksInProgress . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

1171.title: Configuration options
1171.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | E.g. https://vikunja.lan | . | key | string | yes |   | Secret: stays on the server. Settings > API Tokens, with read access to projects and tasks | . | version | number |   | 1 | 2 for Vikunja 1.0.0-rc4 and later | . | enableTaskList | boolean |   | false | The next five tasks by due date as rows | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

1172.title: Filter attributes
1172.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | projects | number | Projects | . | tasks7d | number | Open tasks due within a week | . | tasksOverdue | number | Open tasks past their due date | . | tasksInProgress | number | Open tasks in progress | . | attention | boolean | True while the card marks something as needing attention | .

1173.title: Example
1173.content: # services.yaml - Home: - Vikunja: href: https://vikunja.lan icon: vikunja widget: type: vikunja fields: [projects, tasks7d, tasksOverdue, tasksInProgress] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults url: https://vikunja.lan key: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_VIKUNJA_TOKEN}}" version: 2 enableTaskList: true .

1175.title: Wallos
1175.content: type: wallos · version 0.3.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . Your active subscriptions in Wallos, the next to renew, and what this and next month cost (and with fields last month), as homepage’s wallos widget. The cost is the total of the payments in that month, not a monthly average. With subscriptions in more than one currency set a Fixer API key in Wallos (Settings > Fixer API Key). The API key is under Profile > API Key. Learn more about Wallos.

1176.content: activeSubscriptions, nextRenewingSubscription, previousMonthlyCost, thisMonthlyCost, nextMonthlyCost . Pick them with fields: in the entry; without it the widget shows activeSubscriptions, nextRenewingSubscription, thisMonthlyCost, nextMonthlyCost.

Profile > API Key | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

1178.title: Filter attributes
1178.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | activeSubscriptions | number | Active subscriptions | .

1181.title: Watchtower
1181.content: type: watchtower · version 0.3.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . The containers Watchtower scanned, updated and failed to update (marked) in its last run, as homepage’s watchtower widget. Turn the metrics on with WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_METRICS=true and set a token with WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_TOKEN; give that token as key. The API listens on port 8080 in the container. Learn more about Watchtower.

1182.title: Display fields
1182.content: containers_scanned, containers_updated, containers_failed . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

1183.title: Configuration options
1183.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | E.g. http://watchtower.lan:8080 | . | key | string | yes |   | Secret: stays on the server. WATCHTOWER_HTTP_API_TOKEN | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

1184.title: Filter attributes
1184.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | containers_scanned | number | Containers scanned in the last run | . | containers_updated | number | Containers updated in the last run | . | containers_failed | number | Containers whose update failed in the last run | . | attention | boolean | True while the card marks something as needing attention | .

1185.title: Example

1187.title: wg-easy
1187.content: type: wgeasy · version 0.3.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . The WireGuard clients in wg-easy that are connected (a handshake within threshold minutes, default 2), enabled and in total, and with fields the disabled ones, as homepage’s wgeasy widget. Before wg-easy 15 only the web interface’s password is needed; from 15 set version: 2 and fill in username too. Learn more about wg-easy.

1188.title: Display fields
1188.content: connected, enabled, disabled, total . Pick them with fields: in the entry; without it the widget shows connected, enabled, total.

1189.title: Configuration options
1189.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | E.g. http://wg.lan:51821 | . | version | number |   | 1 | 2 for wg-easy 15 and later | . | username | string |   |   | Wg-easy 15 and later | . | password | string |   |   | Secret: stays on the server. The web interface’s password | . | threshold | number |   | 2 | Minutes since the last handshake that still count as connected | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

1190.title: Filter attributes
1190.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | connected | number | Clients with a handshake within the threshold | . | enabled | number | Clients enabled | . | disabled | number | Clients disabled | . | total | number | Clients in total | .

1191.title: Example
1191.content: # services.yaml - Network: - WireGuard: href: http://wg.lan:51821 icon: wireguard widget: type: wgeasy fields: [connected, enabled, disabled, total] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults url: http://wg.lan:51821 version: 2 username: admin password: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_WGEASY_PASSWORD}}" .

1205.title: Your Spotify
1205.content: type: yourspotify · version 0.3.2 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . The songs you played, how long you listened and how many artists, over the past interval (day, week, month, year or all; default week, the past 7 days), from Your Spotify, as homepage’s yourspotify widget. Generate a public token under Settings > Account > Public token and use the part after ?token= as key. url is Your Spotify’s API (with linuxserver’s image add /api). Learn more about Your Spotify.

1206.title: Display fields
1206.content: songs, time, artists . Pick them with fields: in the entry.

1207.title: Configuration options
1207.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | The API, e.g. http://spotify.lan:8080 (with linuxserver’s image: http://spotify.lan/api) | . | key | string | yes |   | Secret: stays on the server. Settings > Account > Public token: the part after ?token= | . | interval | day / week / month / year / all |   | week |   | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

1208.title: Filter attributes
1208.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | songs | number | Songs played in the interval | . | artists | number | Different artists played in the interval | .

1209.title: Example
1209.content: # services.yaml - Media: - Your Spotify: href: http://spotify.lan icon: spotify widget: type: yourspotify fields: [songs, time, artists] # the display fields; leave out for the defaults url: http://spotify.lan/api key: "{{DASHBOARD_VAR_YOURSPOTIFY_TOKEN}}" interval: month .

1211.title: Zabbix
1211.content: type: zabbix · version 0.3.1 · widget API 2 · Widget collection develop · source . The problems in Zabbix (monitored triggers in a problem state) per severity: warning and average (marked as warnings), high and disaster (marked as errors), and with fields unclassified and information, as homepage’s zabbix widget. Needs Zabbix 7 or later. Create a token under Users > API tokens and use it as key; url is the front end’s address (often ending in /zabbix). Learn more about Zabbix.

1212.title: Display fields
1212.content: unclassified, information, warning, average, high, disaster . Pick them with fields: in the entry; without it the widget shows warning, average, high, disaster.

1213.content: | Option | Type | Required | Default | Description | . | url | url | yes |   | The front end, e.g. http://zabbix.lan/zabbix | . | key | string | yes |   | Secret: stays on the server. Users > API tokens | . Every widget also takes refresh (or refreshInterval in ms), fields and hideErrors; see Services.

1214.title: Filter attributes
1214.content: Public values a service’s filter: can read, as widget.<attribute>; see Filters. | Attribute | Type | Description | . | unclassified | number | Problems of severity unclassified | . | information | number | Problems of severity information | . | warning | number | Problems of severity warning | . | average | number | Problems of severity average | . | high | number | Problems of severity high | . | disaster | number | Problems of severity disaster | . | attention | boolean | True while the card marks something as needing attention | .
